jobs.title: Research Data Analyst II
jobs.description:
Job Description

Job Function Summary

Involves gathering, analyzing, and interpreting a wide variety of research data. Designs and conducts research including selecting data samples, developing research instruments, analyzing collected information according to established statistical methods, and developing recommendations based on research findings. Prepares reports, charts, tables, and other visual aids to interpret and communicate data and results.

Generic Scope

Professional who applies acquired job skills, policies, and procedures to complete substantive assignments / projects / tasks of moderate scope and complexity; exercises judgment within defined guidelines and practices to determine appropriate action.

Custom Scope

This is a part-time (50% FTE) Research Data Analyst position supporting two investigators conducting research on substance use, addiction, and harm reduction services across diverse clinical and community settings. The analyst will contribute to multiple research projects, with a primary focus on data management, statistical analysis, interpretation, and visualization.

The ideal candidate will have training or experience in epidemiology, public health, biostatistics, or a related field, and mixed-methods research skills. Experience working with both large and small datasets, including data cleaning, preparation, management, sycronization, and statistical analysis, is required. Proficiency in R is strongly preferred, particularly for statistical analysis and data visualization, and experience with ArcGIS is desirable. Knowledge of or experience working with harm reduction programs, substance use treatment settings, low-barrier clinics, or populations affected by substance use is preferred. The successful candidate should be comfortable working collaboratively across multiple projects and investigators and translating analytic findings into clear tables, figures, presentations, and manuscripts.

Department Overview

The Division of Prevention Science is a leading force in prevention research innovation. We conduct transformative research, bridging communities and overcoming health inequities through high-impact prevention. The division was established within the Department of Medicine in 1991 and is the administrative home of the Center for AIDS Prevention Studies (CAPS), and the Prevention Research Center (PRC). The division is committed to advancing knowledge in prevention and has extensive expertise in social and behavioral research applied to prevention science and the development of effective prevention interventions across several disease domains. The research focus is risk behavior and reduction; epidemiology of the virus; evaluation of HIV testing procedures, demographic variables and sexual self-identification; and training for providers who care for HIV AIDS patients. While much of the work in DPS has traditionally focused on HIV/AIDS, many investigators are doing important work in other fields including cardiovascular disease, cancer, mental health, and substance abuse. The Division is composed of approximately 35 academics (faculty, fellows and specialists) and 45 non-academic staff who come from a variety of social, behavioral and policy science academic disciplines, including psychology, sociology, anthropology, epidemiology, history, political science, economics, demography, nursing, pharmacy and statistics.

The Division is home to three federally funded research centers that provide valuable infrastructure support: 1) The Center for AIDS Prevention Studies, funded by the National Institute of Mental Health; 2) The UCSF Prevention Research Center, funded by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention; 3) three evaluation centers funded by the Health Resources and Services Administration; and 4) a newly-funded research coordinating center to reduce disparities in multiple chronic diseases, funded by the National Institute on Minority Health and Health Disparities. The Division is also home to the Center of Excellence for Transgender Health and over 100 active sponsored research projects.

Qualifications

Required Qualifications

Experience conducting epidemiological studies using large and small datasets, and working knowledge of research function.
Working skills in statistical analysis, systems programming, database design and data security measures.
Experience in data management and analysis using R and geospatial analysis using ArcGIS software programs.
Communicates complex information in a clear and concise manner both verbally and in writing.
At least one year of experience working with harm reduction organizations, treatment center or low barrier clinics that serve people with a substance use disorder.

Preferred Qualifications

Working skills in conducting interviews and administering surveys (data collection).
Experience working on mixed methods studies that integrates qualitative and quantitative datasets.

Required Education

Bachelor's degree in related area and / or equivalent experience / training.

Preferred Education

Master’s degree in biostatistics, epidemiology or another closely related field.

None listed.

Certifications

None listed.

jobs.title: Senior Data Analyst for Lab Production Support, Extended-Hours Support (ExHS)
jobs.description:
Important: this position will work on the Weekend Shift team, with the following rotation schedules:

Tuesday-to-Saturday (including Tue, Wed, Thur, Fri, and Sat), 9AM-to-5PM.
Sunday-to-Thursday (including Sun, Mon, Tue, Wed, and Thur), 9AM-to-5PM.

This position will rotate through the above work schedules quarterly, i.e., work in one rotation schedule for 3 calendar months, and then move to the other rotation schedule for another 3 calendar months.

This is an exciting opportunity in our Data Science Production Engineering (DSPE) department at Natera (a global leader in precision medicine and genomics testing), to provide critical data analytics support for our lab production operations. As a Senior Data Analyst for Lab Production Support in our DSPE Extended-Hours Support (ExHS) team, you will work in the Weekend Shift team (following the above two rotation schedules). You will have the opportunity to apply innovative data analytics solutions, directly support the most cutting-edge medical diagnostics and genomics applications, and make real & immediate impact to patients and healthcare providers, by providing timely & accurate data analysis support to Natera's production laboratories, as well as for other key business needs.

Primary Responsibilities

Technical Execution and Infrastructure

Deliver timely data support to Lab Operations teams, unblock production issues, and improve patient results turnaround times.
Apply statistical techniques to analyze complex datasets, diagnose operational issues, and support data-driven decision-making.
Perform exploratory data analysis, identify trends, and work with stakeholders to interpret findings and drive continuous improvement.
Design and implement automated solutions for recurring data analysis and production support workflows, improving operational efficiency and scalability.
Extract, transform, and analyze data to generate actionable insights that support lab production operations and business decisions.
Document analytical processes, best practices, and insights to ensure consistency and knowledge transfer across teams.

Process Improvement

Develop and optimize solutions for efficient data retrieval and scalable performance on large and/or complex datasets.
Learn and acquire operational efficiencies on new technologies and solutions developed by other DSPE teams.
Train and coach junior team members on new technologies, procedures, and guidelines/best practices.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

Collaborate with Lab Operations and Product teams to identify process issues, assist with root cause analysis, and provide product support.
Represent the Data Science Production Engineering (DSPE) team in stakeholder meetings.
Effectively and correctly escalate encountered issues to other DSPE teams.

Qualifications

Masters degree in Statistics, Mathematics, Computer Science, Bioinformatics, Operational Research, or other related fields.
Minimum 3 years of relevant industry experience.
Minimum 3 years of experience working in a highly regulated environment (e.g., CLIA and/or FDA compliant settings).
Minimum 3 years of hands-on experience in data analysis, extraction, querying in production support roles.

Knowledge, Skills, And Abilities

Working knowledge of the business processes and requirements of diagnostic laboratories. Knowledge of molecular biology, genetics, genomics, and/or bioinformatics is a plus.
Proficient in data analysis and statistical techniques.
Proficient in Python and SQL development.
Working knowledge of Snowflake platform and cloud technologies.
Strong understanding of statistical concepts such as hypothesis testing, central limit theorem, time series analysis, anomaly detection, and regression modeling.
Good documentation practices and coding style.
Strong verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to present technical findings to both technical and non-technical audiences.
Experience using version control systems such as GitHub or GitLab for managing code and collaboration.
Ability to work collaboratively in a cross-functional team environment.
Strong interpersonal skills.
Strong integrity.

Compensation & Total Rewards

This range reflects a good-faith estimate of the base pay we reasonably expect to offer at the time of hire. Final compensation will vary based on experience, qualifications, and internal equity considerations.

This position is also eligible for additional compensation and benefits through Natera’s robust Total Rewards program, including:

Annual performance incentive bonus
Long-term equity awards
Comprehensive health benefits (medical, dental, vision)
401(k) with company match
Generous paid time off and company holidays
Additional wellness and work-life benefits

Compensation Range

$145,000—$170,000 USD

OUR OPPORTUNITY

Natera™ is a global leader in cell-free DNA (cfDNA) testing, dedicated to oncology, women’s health, and organ health. Our aim is to make personalized genetic testing and diagnostics part of the standard of care to protect health and enable earlier and more targeted interventions that lead to longer, healthier lives.

The Natera team consists of highly dedicated statisticians, geneticists, doctors, laboratory scientists, business professionals, software engineers and many other professionals from world-class institutions, who care deeply for our work and each other. When you join Natera, you’ll work hard and grow quickly. Working alongside the elite of the industry, you’ll be stretched and challenged, and take pride in being part of a company that is changing the landscape of genetic disease management.

What We Offer

Competitive Benefits - Employee benefits include comprehensive medical, dental, vision, life and disability plans for eligible employees and their dependents. Additionally, Natera employees and their immediate families receive free testing in addition to fertility care benefits. Other benefits include pregnancy and baby bonding leave, 401k benefits, commuter benefits and much more. We also offer a generous employee referral program!

jobs.title: R&D Technician
jobs.description:
PsiQuantum's mission is to build the first useful quantum computers: machines capable of delivering the breakthroughs the field has long promised. Since our founding in 2016, our singular focus has been to build and deploy million-qubit, fault-tolerant quantum systems.

Quantum computers harness the laws of quantum mechanics to solve problems that even the most advanced supercomputers or AI systems will never reach. Their impact will span energy, pharmaceuticals, finance, agriculture, transportation, materials, and other foundational industries.

Our architecture and approach is based on silicon photonics. By leveraging the advanced semiconductor manufacturing industry, including partners like GlobalFoundries, we use the same high-volume processes that already produce billions of chips for telecom and consumer electronics. Photonics offers natural advantages for scale: photons don't feel heat, are immune to electromagnetic interference, and integrate with existing cryogenic cooling and standard fiber-optic infrastructure.

That approach has since been tested at the highest level of scrutiny the U.S. government applies to emerging technology, and it has held up. In 2025, PsiQuantum closed a $1 billion funding round that valued the company at $7 billion. In 2026, the U.S. Department of Commerce signed a $100 million Letter of Intent under the CHIPS and Science Act, followed by a $125 million agreement with DARPA under Stage C of its Quantum Benchmarking Initiative, PsiQuantum's most valuable U.S. government agreement to date. This year, we also broke ground on our utility-scale quantum computer in Brisbane, Australia, and continued building out our Chicago site. Victor Peng, our CEO, and co-founder Jeremy O'Brien, now Executive Chairman, lead a team and board that reflects how seriously the world is taking this build, joined this year by Intel's Lip-Bu Tan and Atomico's Niklas Zennström.

PsiQuantum also develops the algorithms and software needed to make these systems commercially valuable. Our application, software, and industry teams work directly with leading Fortune 500 companies, including Airbus, Lockheed Martin, Mercedes-Benz, Boehringer Ingelheim, and Mitsubishi Chemical, to prepare quantum solutions for real-world impact.

Quantum computing is not an extension of classical computing. It represents a fundamental shift, and a path to mastering challenges that cannot be solved any other way. The potential is enormous, and we now have the funding, the government validation, and the sites under construction to make it real.

Job Summary

PsiQuantum is building the world’s first commercially viable quantum computer powered by silicon photonics. Our Foundry Engineering team partners with leading semiconductor manufacturers and research partners to support advanced silicon-based photonic platforms that enable scalable quantum systems.

In this role, you will support day-to-day foundry operations, wafer logistics, wafer inspection, data upload, inventory tracking, documentation, and office/lab coordination activities. This position is hands-on and highly operational, requiring strong attention to detail, clear communication, and consistent follow-through across multiple systems, tools, and partner sites.

The ideal candidate will be organized, dependable, comfortable working with wafers and lab/office workflows, and able to support engineering teams by keeping wafer movement, documentation, inspection records, reports, and operational communications accurate and up to date. You will work closely with PsiQuantum engineers, operations teams, and other external partners to help ensure smooth execution of wafer processing and foundry-related activities.

Responsibilities

Support wafer handling activities, including FOSB mapping, wafer transfers, lot start documentation, and delivery of required documentation and materials to clean room.
Maintain accurate wafers in process (WIP) reports, wafer/FOSB inventory records and related tracking updates.
Update tool status and WIP reports twice per day and communicate key updates to the team.
Attend operations morning meetings, take clear notes, and distribute relevant action items, status updates, and operational information to the team.
Coordinate wafer and package logistics, including wafer shipments, shipping contacts, package pickup from Shipping & Receiving, and maintenance of shipping addresses, emails, and phone numbers.
Support lab, office, and partner-site operations, including lab activities, SP3 data collection and other operational systems.
Manage and operate a dedicated lab for wafer cryogenic testing including sample preparation, material acquisition, minor maintenance and remaining logistics needs.
Inspect wafers using optical microscopy, capture wafer images, and upload images and related records to support the engineering team.
Maintain an orderly office and shared work environment, including purchasing and restocking office supplies, lab supplies, snacks, and other recurring items for the regional offices.

Experience/Qualifications

High school diploma or equivalent required; associate degree, technical certification, or relevant semiconductor, manufacturing, or laboratory experience preferred.
Experience working in a semiconductor, cleanroom, laboratory, manufacturing, logistics, or technical operations environment required.
Strong attention to detail and ability to follow documented procedures accurately.
Comfortable handling wafers, wafer carriers, FOSBs, documentation packages, and related materials.
Ability to use inspection tools, capture images, upload files, and maintain accurate digital records.
Familiarity with wafer tracking systems, work request systems, inventory systems, or manufacturing execution systems is preferred.
Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple daily tasks, recurring reports, shipments, supplies, and documentation workflows.
Clear written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to summarize meeting notes and share updates through Slack or similar communication platforms.
Ability to work independently, escalate issues appropriately, and support engineers and operations teams in a fast-paced technical environment.
Proficiency with basic computer tools such as Microsoft Office, spreadsheets, file upload systems, and web-based workflow tools.
Dependable, hands-on, and proactive approach to maintaining operational readiness, inventory accuracy, and an orderly work environment.

jobs.title: Research Associate, Technology Development
jobs.description:
About AtlasBase

AtlasBase is a fast-growing pioneer in Molecular Computing, bridging the gap between traditional IT and biotechnology. We are redefining global IT infrastructure by driving breakthroughs in both Molecular Compute and Molecular Data Storage. By commercializing synthetic DNA-based technologies at IT scale, AtlasBase delivers ultra-high-density, low-maintenance, and carbon-conscious solutions built for the explosive growth and value of the world's data. Leveraging nature’s most durable medium, we provide a virtually permanent foundation that transforms how the world processes and secures its most critical information.

Originally spun out of Twist Bioscience, our team is an elite fusion of scientists, engineers, and operators dedicated to solving some of the most complex infrastructure challenges on Earth. While our work is grounded in deep science, our success depends on world-class talent across every discipline. We are seeking a Research Associate, Technology Development

who is ready to bring their expertise to a high-impact environment and help us build a brand-new category of technology.

About The Role

In this role you will perform, analyze, and interpret the characterization of our nanoelectronic semiconductor devices at various stages of their lifecycle. Such characterization makes up a crucial part of our quality control process to ensure received devices meet the required specifications and also provides crucial feedback following experimentation as part of our test and learning cycles. The ideal candidate will have a strong background in Physics, Materials Science and or Nanotechnology, be rigorous and detail oriented, work well within a highly interdisciplinary environment and be eager to learn and contribute.

Responsibilities

Perform characterization of devices using a wide range of metrology techniques including atomic force microscopy (AFM), photoinduced force microscopy (PiFM), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), and nanoelectronic measurements.
Work closely with outside vendors, collaborators, and fabrication partners to coordinate the characterization of devices using techniques such as time-of-flight mass spectroscopy (TOF-SIM/nano-SIMs), x-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), transmission electron microscopy (TEM), and Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR).
Prepare reports on pristine (as received) nanoelectronic devices using the techniques listed above as part of our standard quality control processes.
Prepare experimental summaries characterizing devices after various experiments to provide feedback as part of our test and learning cycles.
Understand the requirements of our nanoelectronic devices and propose characterization techniques to ensure devices meet these specifications.
Maintain detailed and meticulous records of all experimental work and analysis.
Effectively communicate experimental results, data analysis, and next steps with our chip fabrication, device measurements, surface chemistry teams, and the wider company.

Qualifications

Bachelor's or Master’s degree in Physics, Materials Science, Nanotechnology or a closely related field with >0-3 years of relevant industry experience.
Some experience using advanced metrology techniques such as AFM, SEM, TEM, XPS, FTIR, or TOF-SIMs.
Understanding of electron transport physics and electrochemistry, ideally at nanoelectrodes.
Strong data analysis and scripting experience is desirable.
Experience working in the semiconductor industry or biotechnology is a plus.
Must be a creative and detail-oriented person with excellent analytical, verbal, and written communication skills.
Exceptional collaboration skills and ability to work seamlessly in a dynamic and fast-paced environment.

Physical Demands & Work Environment

Work will be performed onsite in office and laboratory space located in South San Francisco.
Mobility: Must be able to move about the laboratory and office environment regularly. This includes standing and walking for extended periods, often up to 6–8 hours per day.
Manual Dexterity: Must have fine motor skills and steady hands to handle delicate instruments, operate laboratory equipment, pipette accurately, and perform repetitive benchwork with precision.
Lifting/Carrying: Must be able to lift and carry up to 40 pounds occasionally, such as boxes of lab supplies or equipment.
Visual Acuity: Must have sufficient visual acuity to read small print on labels, instrument displays, and computer monitors. Close vision, color vision, and the ability to adjust focus are required.
Environmental Conditions: Frequently exposed to typical laboratory conditions, including biological samples, chemicals, and reagents. Must be able to wear appropriate personal protective equipment (PPE) such as lab coats, gloves, and safety goggles as required.

80,000 - 110,000 USD per year(HQ)

Job Title: Quality Control Technician Battery Materials
Job Description

The Quality Control Technician for battery materials is responsible for screening, characterizing, and performing quality control on raw materials that support electrode and cell development programs. In this role, you operate a suite of analytical instruments to generate high-quality materials data that directly informs purchasing decisions, supplier qualification, and formulation development. This position suits someone who enjoys detailed, measurement-intensive work, takes pride in producing reliable analytical data, and helps keep materials programs running smoothly.

Responsibilities

Perform incoming materials characterization on raw materials and make clear pass or fail determinations against established acceptance criteria.
Operate analytical instruments for materials characterization, including particle size analyzers, BET surface area analyzers, X-ray diffraction (XRD), scanning electron microscopy with energy-dispersive spectroscopy (SEM/EDS), thermal analysis instruments such as TGA and DSC, slurry rheology equipment, and conductivity measurement tools.
Carry out wet chemistry sample preparation and analysis, including titration and related techniques, to support materials characterization.
Prepare materials samples using techniques such as milling, drying, pressing, and cross-sectioning to ensure consistent and reliable analysis.
Maintain and update the materials inventory database, ensuring accurate tracking of raw materials and test results.
Support supplier qualification by generating comparative characterization datasets across different vendor samples and summarizing findings.
Generate clear characterization reports, data summaries, and tables that communicate results to internal stakeholders.
Escalate anomalous results, unexpected trends, or potential instrument performance issues promptly to ensure timely investigation and resolution.
Perform routine instrument maintenance, calibration, and troubleshooting on analytical equipment to ensure consistent and accurate performance.
Maintain calibration logs, standard reference trackers, and standard operating procedure (SOP) documentation, and coordinate service calls with external providers as needed.
Follow all chemical hygiene, personal protective equipment (PPE), and safety protocols while working with materials and analytical instruments.
Manage consumables inventory, including chemicals, standards, and lab supplies, to support uninterrupted laboratory operations.
Keep characterization laboratory spaces clean, organized, and compliant with safety and quality standards.
Contribute to the writing, review, and updating of SOPs to reflect best practices and continuous improvement in laboratory processes.

Essential Skills

13 years of hands-on experience operating analytical instruments in a materials, chemistry, or battery laboratory environment; internship experience counts toward this requirement.
Strong background in chemistry or analytical chemistry, with practical laboratory experience.
Proficiency with materials characterization techniques such as particle size analysis, BET surface area analysis, X-ray diffraction (XRD), SEM/EDS, thermal analysis (TGA/DSC), and rheometry or slurry rheology.
Experience with materials sample preparation techniques, including milling, drying, pressing, and cross-sectioning.
High attention to detail and a methodical approach to measurement and data collection.
Demonstrated commitment to data quality, including careful documentation, verification, and review of results.
Ability to read, interpret, and implement standard operating procedures (SOPs) accurately.
Capability to contribute to the drafting and updating of SOPs based on laboratory experience and process improvements.
Knowledge of laboratory safety practices, including safe chemical handling, PPE requirements, and emergency procedures.
Ability to operate and maintain analytical instruments, perform routine calibrations, and troubleshoot basic equipment issues.
Strong organizational skills for maintaining inventory databases, calibration logs, and laboratory documentation.

Additional Skills & Qualifications

Academic or practical training in materials science, chemistry, chemical engineering, or a related discipline.
Experience working in a battery, energy storage, or advanced materials laboratory environment.
Familiarity with generating comparative datasets to support supplier qualification and material selection.
Experience writing clear technical reports, summary tables, and documentation for internal stakeholders.
Comfort working in a fast-paced, data-driven environment where analytical results inform purchasing and development decisions.

Work Environment

This role is fully onsite in a laboratory environment in San Leandro. You work primarily in a hands-on lab setting with analytical instruments such as particle size analyzers, BET surface area analyzers, XRD, SEM/EDS, TGA/DSC, rheometers, and conductivity measurement systems. The position involves regular handling of chemicals and materials, so you follow established chemical hygiene practices and use appropriate personal protective equipment (PPE) at all times. The lab environment emphasizes cleanliness, organization, and adherence to safety protocols, with structured documentation, calibration logs, and SOPs guiding daily work. You collaborate closely with technical teams involved in electrode and cell development, contributing data that supports material selection, supplier qualification, and formulation optimization.

jobs.title: Quality Control Lab Technician
jobs.description:
Job Title: Quality Control Lab Technician

Job Description

The Quality Control Lab Technician supports a high-volume manufacturing operation by performing accurate and timely quality testing on raw materials, bulk batches, and finished products. This role ensures that products meet strict specifications, communicates test results and batch adjustments clearly to production operators, and initiates investigations into non-conforming materials. The position offers strong long-term growth potential for someone who is proactive, detail-oriented, and eager to streamline testing processes and advance into higher-level technical roles over time.

Schedule: Thursday- Monday or Friday-Tuesday (8 am - 5 pm) or (7 am-4 pm)

Responsibilities

Execute and adhere to all environmental, health, and safety (EHS) requirements, maintaining a safe work environment and following internal safety rules and procedures, including wearing appropriate personal protective equipment (PPE).
Participate in the general housekeeping of the plant and laboratory areas to maintain a clean, organized, and compliant workspace.
Comply with all company policies, procedures, and quality standards in daily activities.
Perform timely and accurate chemical, physical, and visual testing on raw materials, bulk batches, and finished goods using standard test procedures.
Determine raw material adjustment amounts for bulk batches to ensure products meet required specifications.
Enter test results for raw materials, bulk batches, and finished goods into the ERP system (SAP) accurately and promptly.
Perform timely usage decisions (accept or reject) for raw materials, bulk batches, and finished goods in SAP based on test results and specifications.
Collect and store retain samples of raw materials, bulk batches, and finished products as required for traceability and future investigations.
Take immediate action on internal non-conformances by creating notifications in SAP and performing initial investigations in collaboration with production operators.
Support customer complaint investigations by reviewing batch records, analyzing retain samples, and contributing to root cause analysis and corrective actions.
Maintain critical laboratory equipment, including routine checks and basic troubleshooting, to support continuous and uninterrupted quality control testing.
Monitor and maintain laboratory inventory of reagents, consumables, and supplies to ensure consistent testing capability.
Review the daily production schedule and ensure that test equipment, reagents, and methods are prepared to efficiently test all scheduled batches.
Provide accurate documentation and visual quality control labels for materials and products that are acceptable, rejected, or on hold.
Issue, complete, maintain, and process all relevant paperwork and records related to testing, non-conformances, and quality documentation.
Participate in monthly meetings focused on quality, safety, housekeeping, and waste minimization, contributing ideas for continuous improvement.
Communicate all critical issues and problems concerning quality control test equipment, potential testing delays, and quality risks promptly to management.
Act as a proactive team player by volunteering to help where needed, supporting colleagues, and contributing to shared goals.
Apply lean manufacturing and continuous improvement principles, including participation in audits, root cause and corrective action activities, and documentation updates.
Manage multiple testing tasks and projects concurrently, demonstrating strong time management and prioritization skills in a laboratory setting.
Serve as a reliable gatekeeper for production quality by responding quickly to issues, ensuring that non-conforming material is identified and addressed immediately.

Essential Skills

Bachelor of Science degree in Chemical Engineering or Chemistry.
Minimum of 1+ years of experience, which may include internships or early-career roles, preferably in aerospace, manufacturing, or consumer products environments.
Hands-on experience performing chemical, physical, and visual testing in a laboratory or production support setting.
Proficiency with ERP systems, specifically SAP, including entering test results and making usage decisions.
Working knowledge of Microsoft Excel, Microsoft Teams, and Microsoft Outlook for data management, communication, and coordination.

jobs.title: Lab Technician 2
jobs.description:
Hiring a Lab Technician for a great company in Fresno, CA. Looking for at least 6 months to a year of prior lab experience.

Job Description

The Lab Technician plays a key role in supporting complex microbiological studies and procedures within a food microbiology laboratory operating under Good Laboratory Practice (GLP) conditions. This position focuses on producing accurate, traceable, and defendable results while working with a variety of organisms, including pathogens and spore crops. The Lab Technician collaborates closely with microbiologists and other laboratory staff, contributes to experiment execution, and helps maintain a safe, organized, and efficient laboratory environment.

Responsibilities

Use proper handling procedures and aseptic techniques to ensure the integrity and safety of all microbiological work.
Assist with the setup, scheduling, preparation, and execution of complex studies and procedures in accordance with GLP conditions.
Produce accurate, traceable, and defendable results within established timelines and quality standards.
Work with and maintain a variety of organisms, including pathogens and spore crops, following appropriate safety and handling protocols.
Assist microbiologists in conducting experiments and support the design and execution of microbiological studies.
Conduct experiments and studies that may involve Clostridium botulinum, adhering to all relevant safety and procedural guidelines.
Perform routine and non-routine laboratory tasks under general supervision to ensure supervisor and client satisfaction.
Carry out microbial transfers using aseptic techniques to prevent contamination and ensure reliable results.
Perform microbial identification and enumeration techniques to support food microbiology analyses.
Accurately prepare media and reagents required for microbiological testing and experimental work.
Pour plates, perform serial dilutions, and carry out pipetting procedures with precision and consistency.
Conduct microscopic observations, including direct microscopic counts, gram stains, and wet mounts.
Operate necessary laboratory equipment as required for assigned projects, ensuring correct and safe usage.
Maintain instruments and equipment so they remain continuously in good working order, including routine checks and basic maintenance.
Identify and communicate equipment and facility improvement opportunities or issues to the supervisor in a timely manner.
Maintain a safe and orderly work environment by following laboratory safety practices and housekeeping standards.
Maintain good working communication with all staff to support effective teamwork and information sharing.
Follow appropriate standard operating procedures (SOPs) and protocols as instructed by the supervisor.
Maintain detailed, accurate laboratory and experimental records to ensure data traceability and compliance.
Work as a team member with all staff to accomplish position objectives and broader business goals.
Assist in training or mentoring laboratory staff as needed, sharing knowledge of methods and best practices.
Troubleshoot laboratory methods, equipment issues, and nonconforming results to help maintain quality and reliability.
Perform other laboratory-related tasks as assigned to support ongoing projects and operational needs.

Essential Skills

Associates degree in a scientific discipline; a Bachelors degree is preferred.
At least 4 years of food microbiology laboratory experience.
Demonstrated proficiency in independently performing routine and complex microbiological analyses.
Strong practical knowledge of aseptic techniques and proper handling procedures for microbiological work.
Experience working with a variety of organisms, including pathogens and spore crops, in a laboratory setting.
Ability to accurately perform microbial transfers, identification, and enumeration techniques.
Hands-on experience preparing media and reagents, including plate pouring, dilutions, and pipetting.
Proficiency in microscopic observations, including direct microscopic counts, gram staining, and wet mounts.
Ability to operate and maintain common laboratory instruments and equipment used in microbiology.
Experience troubleshooting laboratory methods, equipment performance, and nonconforming results.
Strong documentation skills with the ability to maintain clear, accurate, and traceable laboratory records.
Solid organization skills to manage multiple tasks, studies, and deadlines effectively.
Effective communication skills to interact with supervisors, microbiologists, and laboratory staff.
Ability to follow GLP requirements, SOPs, and protocols consistently.
Willingness and ability to work overtime, weekends, and holidays as required by project needs.

Additional Skills & Qualifications

Bachelors degree in a relevant scientific discipline is preferred.
Experience training or mentoring laboratory staff in microbiological techniques and procedures.
Experience in food microbiology, including familiarity with industry standards and testing methods.
Experience conducting or supporting studies involving Clostridium botulinum or similar pathogens.
Strong attention to detail and commitment to producing defendable and high-quality data.
Ability to collaborate effectively in a team-oriented environment and contribute to shared objectives.
Comfort working under general supervision while taking responsibility for assigned tasks.
Capability to identify and propose improvements to laboratory equipment, workflows, and facilities.

Work Environment

The role is based in a food microbiology laboratory that operates under Good Laboratory Practice (GLP) conditions, with a strong emphasis on safety, cleanliness, and data integrity. The Lab Technician works with various microorganisms, including pathogens and spore crops, and uses equipment such as incubators, microscopes, pipettes, and other standard microbiology instruments. The environment is highly collaborative, with close interaction among microbiologists and laboratory staff to support complex studies and routine testing. Detailed record-keeping, adherence to SOPs, and continuous equipment maintenance are core aspects of daily work. The schedule may include overtime, weekend, and holiday hours to meet project timelines and client requirements. Appropriate laboratory attire and personal protective equipment are used to maintain a safe and orderly workspace.

Supermicro® is a Top Tier provider of advanced server, storage, and networking solutions for Data Center, Cloud Computing, Enterprise IT, Hadoop/ Big Data, Hyperscale, HPC and IoT/Embedded customers worldwide. We seek talented, passionate, and committed engineers, technologists, and business leaders to join us.

Job Summary

This is a forward-deployed architecture role. You will work with the customer for discovery, workshops, and proofs of concept. You design the AI factory, stand the first system up with the customer’s team, and stay involved through production handoff. You will package the design so Supermicro can repeat and scale it across thousands of customers. You will work with Supermicro sales, factory engineering, and NVIDIA field architects.

Supermicro partners with NVIDIA, AMD, and Intel, and with leading storage and networking companies. Most work on these accounts is NVIDIA-based — HGX, NVL-class systems, and NVIDIA software. AMD, Intel, storage, and networking included when the customer’s standard requires it.

This position is located in San Jose, CA. Exceptional candidates elsewhere in the United States will be considered if candidate can travel extensively for customer deployments.

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

Forward-deployed customer architecture

Embed with high-profile Life Sciences, Healthcare, or Financial Services accounts for discovery and design. Sit with scientists, risk, infrastructure, and security. Analyze the workload on their data and constraints. Produce the architecture and present it to executives and technical teams. Package departmental GPU and HPC nodes, HGX-class clusters, or rack-scale NVL systems, including networking, power, and liquid cooling.

Workshop, POC, and production handoff Run workshops from workload and data boundary to architecture, TCO, and operating model. Scope and run the proof of concept on Supermicro hardware, bring-up, workload, fail-closed tests. Write the production design Supermicro can build and ship. Bring in AI safety best practices when agents or sensitive data are in scope. Stay involved through first production handoff, then return the repeatable design to scale across similar customers.
Enablement and field leadership Document what worked at the account so the next deal in the vertical does not start from zero. Train sales and field engineers on how these accounts buy and deploy. Represent Supermicro with customers, partners, and at industry events in Life Sciences, Healthcare, or Financial Services.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s or master’s degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Information Technology, or equivalent. 12+ years as a solution architect, data center architect, or consultant, with production deployments you can point to.
Experience designing hybrid AI or HPC estates: private / on-prem plus public cloud and/or GPU cloud / neocloud. Comfortable working on the customer floor: workshops, lab bring-up, and POC execution, not only remote design reviews.
Experience taking large GPU/HPC systems from first workshop to production, including networking and data center power and cooling. Working knowledge of NVIDIA data center GPU platforms and software. NVIDIA certification is desirable.
Working knowledge of AMD and Intel server platforms and of major storage and networking products. Experience with regulated data, on-premises inference, or scientific computing is strongly preferred. Ability to travel to customer sites for multi-day workshops and POCs.

jobs.title: Research Assistant, Integrated Genomics Operation
jobs.description:
About Us

The people of Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center (MSK) are united by a singular mission: ending cancer for life. Our specialized care teams provide personalized, compassionate, expert care to patients of all ages. Informed by basic research done at our Sloan Kettering Institute, scientists across MSK collaborate to conduct innovative translational and clinical research that is driving a revolution in our understanding of cancer as a disease and improving the ability to prevent, diagnose, and treat it. MSK is dedicated to training the next generation of scientists and clinicians, who go on to pursue our mission at MSK and around the globe.

Exciting opportunity at MSK: Join our Integrated Genomics Operation
team as a Research Assistant
!

The Integrated Genomics Operation (IGO) enables basic, clinical and translational research projects across the Cancer Center. IGO implements the MSK mission to cure cancer by providing a broad range of genomic services and expertise to our world-class research scientists. We are a high throughput core facility producing >100TB of data per year across >40 applications including “fourth generation” of genomics technologies such as single cell and spatial transcriptomics.

The IGO “Seq Team” provides cutting-edge sequencing chemistries to MSK investigators, from Illumina, Oxford Nanopore and Element Biosciences. We seek an experienced bench scientist who is enthusiastic about mastering a wide range of sequencing applications. The candidate will learn all the nuances of assessing library quality and quantity, learn how to combine different types of samples on to a flowcell and assess sequencing data quality. IGO has a strong team-based culture and as such, the candidate will interface with many other teams within the lab. Prior experience with sequencing is welcome but not required, in-depth training will be provided regardless!

Role Overview

Operate short-read (Illumina, Element) and long-read (Oxford Nanopore) sequencers.
Assist the group leader in planning sequencing runs.
Execute QC and pooling processes for sequencing libraries.
Evaluate QC results and troubleshoot as required.
Manage sequencing reagent inventory in collaboration with lab management.
Maintain documentation in the IGO Laboratory Information Management System (LIMS).
Communicate with scientists and vendor technical support and sales representatives.
Collaborate across IGO teams to ensure smooth sample processing and data transfer.
Learn to operate liquid handlers and robotic instrument for high-throughput workflows.

Key Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree with at least 4 years of relevant experience or Master’s degree with 2 years of experience.
Strong foundation in molecular biology.
Genomics experience is a plus.

Core Skills

Exceptional attention to detail and strong analytical skills.
Ability to thrive in a fast-paced research environment, managing multiple projects while maintaining precision. Enthusiastic about learning opportunities in the lab.
Critical thinking and problem-solving skills to troubleshoot experimental challenges.
Outstanding interpersonal and communication skills and the ability to interact across all levels in a confident, concise, professional manner.
Enthusiasm and dedication to MSK's vision, mission, and values.

jobs.description:
Company Description

Join us and make YOUR mark on the World!

Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory (LLNL) has turned bold ideas into world-changing impact advancing science and technology to strengthen U.S. security and promote global stability.

Our mission spans four critical national security areas nuclear deterrence, threat preparedness, energy security, and multi-domain defense empowering teams to take on the toughest challenges of today and tomorrow. With a culture built on innovation and operational excellence, LLNL is a place where your expertise can make a real impact.

Job Description

We are seeking a Postdoctoral Researcher
to develop novel, correlative microanalytical techniques for forensic characterization of nuclear materials, with a focus on developing approaches for nuclear materials characterization across a range of spatial scales. This position leverages LLNL’s state-of-the-art suite of secondary ion mass spectrometry (SIMS), electron microscopy and other complementary instruments to build upon previous research investigating lateral mixing quantification, age dating, and correlative image fusion methodologies. This position is in the Trace Isotope and Element Signatures group of the Nuclear and Chemical Sciences Division.

This position requires full-time on-site presence due to the nature of the work.

You will

Use SIMS instruments (e.g., NanoSIMS and Small Geometry SIMS) for high-resolution isotopic imaging.
Use electron microscopy instruments (secondary electron microscopy [SEM], energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy [EDS] and transmission electron microscopy [TEM]) for elemental and morphological characterization.
Employ artificial intelligence and machine learning (AI/ML) tools to analyze and interpret microanalytical image datasets.
Apply statistical methods for uncertainty quantification in microanalytical measurements.
Publish research results in high-impact, peer-reviewed scientific or technical journals.
Present findings at external conferences, seminars, and/or technical meetings within the nuclear forensics community.
Collaborate with others in a multidisciplinary team environment to accomplish research goals.
Perform other duties as assigned.

Qualifications

Ability to secure and maintain a U.S. DOE Q-level security clearance, which requires U.S. Citizenship.
PhD in analytical chemistry, geochemistry, materials science, or related field.
Experience with microanalysis methods, such as SIMS, SEM, EDS and TEM.
Strong foundation in mass spectrometry principles.
Ability to develop independent research projects as demonstrated through peer-reviewed publications.
Programming experience in Python or similar environments for data analysis, visualization and/or automation.
Innovative experimental skills with experience in experimental design, technique development, and execution.
Capability to work independently and collaboratively in multidisciplinary research environments.
Proficient written and verbal communication skills for delivering presentations, preparing publications and writing technical reports.

Qualifications We Desire

Experience with correlative microanalytical techniques and/or multi-modal imaging approaches.
Knowledge of nuclear forensics concepts, material production processes and/or nuclear fuel cycle science.

jobs.title: Post Doctorate Research Associate - Chemical Physics in Experimental X-Ray Scattering
jobs.description:
Overview

At PNNL, our core capabilities are divided among major departments that we refer to as Directorates within the Lab, focused on a specific area of scientific research or other function, with its own leadership team and dedicated budget.

Our Science & Technology directorates include National Security, Integrated Discovery Sciences, and Energy and Environment. In addition, we have an Environmental Molecular Sciences Laboratory, a Department of Energy, Office of Science user facility housed on the PNNL campus.

The Integrated Discovery Sciences Directorate (IDSD) leads fundamental research across biology, chemistry, earth and environmental sciences, materials science, advanced computing, artificial intelligence, quantum information science, mathematics, autonomy, and DOE national user facilities. Our vision is to accelerate scientific discovery by observing, understanding, simulating, predicting, and controlling dynamic biotic-abiotic processes and interactions within complex biological, chemical, material, and Earth systems. We intentionally connect disciplines to advance fundamental discovery science, develop transformative scientific capabilities, and address the nation's most important challenges in energy, environmental resilience, biotechnology, advanced manufacturing, health, and national security.

Responsibilities

Contribute to PNNL’s goals as part of the Lab’s Physical Sciences Division (PSD). Through fundamental research supported by DOE Basic Energy Sciences, we seek to understand the fundamental interactions, reactivity, and dynamics of ions in solutions, that are relevant for a multitude of energy and biological processes. The proposed research effort focuses on developing and utilizing advanced X-ray scattering methods, in particular X-ray Photon Correlation Spectroscopy (XPCS), to probe with atomic scale resolution the equilibrium and non-equilibrium atomic structure of complex ionic solutions and solvated molecular complexes. These experiments will be strongly coupled with state-of-the art theoretical efforts for the interpretation and modelling of the data.

As a postdoctoral researcher based in the experimental Physical Chemistry group, you will investigate challenging molecular-scale science questions, including ion-solvent and ion-ion interactions and dynamics, the mechanisms of charge and proton transfer in molecules, and the spontaneous collective fluctuations that drive chemical reactivity in liquids. You will conduct split-pulse XPCS and related experiments using the LCLS X-ray Free Electron laser (XFEL) at the SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory and related XFELs and synchrotron facilities around the world. You will be mentored and collaborate with other senior investigators in a multi-institutional team, including researchers at PNNL, and SLAC. This position is based at SLAC (Menlo Park, CA).

What You Will Do

Propose, lead, and participate in X-ray experiments at large-scale X-ray light source facilities to investigate the structure and dynamics of ionic solutions.
Perform extensive analysis of complex datasets, including learning and developing the computational tools and analysis codes necessary to extract structural and dynamical information from X-ray scattering experiments.
Interpret experimental data through comparison with state-of-the-art theoretical calculations, in close collaboration with members of the theory team.
Work independently, take initiative, and contribute effectively to collaborative, interdisciplinary research projects.
Prepare and publish manuscripts in peer-reviewed scientific journals.
Become an integral member of PNNL and SLAC fundamental chemical physics research teams, taking advantage of world-class expertise and capabilities to advance your research. Interact, communicate, and problem-solve with researchers across the multi-institutional collaboration.
Present research findings at scientific conferences, workshops, and project/program review meetings.

Qualifications

Minimum Qualifications:

Candidates must have received a PhD within the past five years (60 months) or within the next 8 months from an accredited college or university.

Preferred Qualifications

Ph.D. in Physical Chemistry, Physics, Materials Science, or a related field.
Experience with XPCS or X-ray scattering methods at synchrotrons or XFELs and/or experience with tabletop ultrafast spectroscopy methods.
Strong ability to analyze complex datasets and develop appropriate models, working closely with theorists; familiarity with coding languages such as Python and/or Julia.
Strong critical-thinking and problem-solving skills, with the ability to take initiative, identify new research opportunities, and independently develop solutions to challenging scientific problems.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
Strong leadership abilities and the ability to work effectively as part of an interdisciplinary team of scientists across multiple institutions.
Ability to travel from SLAC to PNNL for regular meetings with PNNL researchers, and to synchrotron and XFEL facilities around the world to perform experiments.

Hazardous Working Conditions/Environment

Standard laboratory hazards.

Testing Designated Position

This is not a Testing Designated Position (TDP).

About PNNL

Pacific Northwest National Laboratory (PNNL) is a world-class research institution powered by a highly educated, diverse workforce committed to the values of Integrity, Creativity, Collaboration, Impact, and Courage. Every year, scores of dynamic, driven people come to PNNL to work with renowned researchers on meaningful science, innovations and outcomes for the U.S. Department of Energy and other sponsors; here is your chance to be one of them!

At PNNL, you will find an exciting research environment and excellent benefits including health insurance, and flexible work schedules. PNNL is located in eastern Washington State—the dry side of Washington known for its stellar outdoor recreation and affordable cost of living. The Lab’s campus is only a 45-minute flight (or ~3 hour drive) from Seattle or Portland, and is serviced by the convenient PSC airport, connected to 8 major hubs.

Commitment to Excellence and Equal Employment Opportunity

Our laboratory is committed to fostering a work environment where all individuals are treated with fairness and respect while solving critical challenges in fundamental sciences, national security, and energy resiliency. We are an Equal Employment Opportunity employer.

Pacific Northwest National Laboratory (PNNL) is an Equal Opportunity Employer. PNNL considers all applicants for employment without regard to race, religion, color, sex, national origin, age, disability, genetic information (including family medical history), protected veteran status, and any other status or characteristic protected by federal, state, and/or local laws.

We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations for individuals with disabilities and disabled veterans in our job application procedures and in employment. If you need assistance or an accommodation due to a disability, contact us at careers@pnnl.gov.

Drug Free Workplace

PNNL is committed to a drug-free workplace supported by Workplace Substance Abuse Program (WSAP) and complies with federal laws prohibiting the possession and use of illegal drugs.

If you are offered employment at PNNL, you must pass a drug test prior to commencing employment. PNNL complies with federal law regarding illegal drug use. Under federal law, marijuana remains an illegal drug. If you test positive for any illegal controlled substance, including marijuana, your offer of employment will be withdrawn.

Security, Credentialing, And Eligibility Requirements

As a national laboratory, PNNL is responsible for adhering to the Homeland Security Presidential Directive 12 (HSPD-12) and Department of Energy (DOE) Order 473.1A, which require new employees to obtain and maintain a HSPD-12 Personal Identify Verification (PIV) Credential. To obtain this credential, new employees must successfully complete the applicable tier of federal background investigation post hire and receive a favorable federal adjudication. The tier of federal background investigation will be determined by job duties and national security or public trust responsibilities associated with the job. All tiers of investigation include a declaration of illegal drug activities, including use, supply, possession, or manufacture within the last 1 to 7 years (depending on the applicable tier of investigation). Illegal drug activities include marijuana and cannabis derivatives, which are still considered illegal under federal law, regardless of state laws.

For Foreign National Candidates

If you have not resided in the U.S. for three consecutive years, you are not eligible for the PIV credential and instead will need to obtain a favorable Local Site Specific Only (LSSO) Federal risk determination to maintain employment. Once you meet the three-year residency requirement thereafter, you will be required to obtain a PIV credential to maintain employment. The tier of federal background investigation required to obtain the PIV credential will be determined by job duties at the time you become eligible for the PIV credential.

Mandatory Requirements

Please be aware that the Department of Energy (DOE) prohibits DOE employees and contractors from having any affiliation with the foreign government of a country DOE has identified as a “country of risk” without explicit approval by DOE and Battelle. If you are offered a position at PNNL and currently have any affiliation with the government of one of these countries, you will be required to disclose this information and recuse yourself of that affiliation or receive approval from DOE and Battelle prior to your first day of employment.

Rockstar Rewards

Employees and their families are offered medical insurance, dental insurance, vision insurance, robust telehealth care options, several mental health benefits, free wellness coaching, health savings account, flexible spending accounts, basic life insurance, disability insurance*, employee assistance program, business travel insurance, tuition assistance, relocation, backup childcare, legal benefits, supplemental parental bonding leave, surrogacy and adoption assistance, and fertility support. Employees are automatically enrolled in our company-funded pension plan* and may enroll in our 401 (k) savings plan with company match*. Employees may accrue up to 120 vacation hours per year and may receive ten paid holidays per year.

Research Associates excluded.
All benefits are dependent upon eligibility.

Starting pay is calculated from the minimum of the pay range and actual placement in the range is determined based on an individual’s relevant job-related skills, qualifications, and experience. This approach is applicable to all positions, with the exception of positions governed by collective bargaining agreements and certain limited-term positions which have specific pay rules.

AI coding agents are an important part of the engineering workflow, but strong fundamentals, critical thinking, and rigorous validation remain essential. Accountabilities

Design, develop, test, and deploy end-to-end features spanning AWS infrastructure, Python and Java backend services, agentic LLM workflows, and Angular/TypeScript frontends.
Build and evolve AI workflows using Amazon Bedrock, including function and tool calling, RAG, embeddings, prompt design, validation loops, and production fallback strategies.

Bachelor’s degree in Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a related discipline; a master’s degree is preferred.
10+ years of professional software development experience, ideally working with enterprise server, storage, networking, or similarly complex technology products.
Strong Python development skills, including modern typing, asynchronous programming, data validation frameworks such as Pydantic, structured error handling, and maintainable large-scale code organization.
Deep Java backend expertise with Spring Boot and/or Quarkus, clean architecture, strong use of the type system, and experience with modern concurrency concepts such as Java virtual threads.

Practical experience developing LLM-powered applications, including function calling, prompt engineering, RAG, embeddings, agent workflows, and systematic evaluation of AI-generated outputs.
Experience building modern Angular/TypeScript frontends that consume production APIs.
Familiarity with Docker, Docker Swarm and/or Kubernetes, Git, Azure DevOps pipelines, code review, and multi-repository development environments.
Strong understanding of software testing, including unit testing, integration testing, mocking, and quality practices suitable for production systems.
Experience with secure coding, authentication, structured logging, tracing, metrics, operational analytics, and production observability.
Ability to work effectively with AI-assisted development tools such as Claude, Kiro, or comparable agentic IDEs/CLIs while independently understanding, reviewing, debugging, and correcting generated code.
Strong specification-driven development skills, with the ability to decompose complex requirements into clear designs, tasks, constraints, and acceptance criteria.
Strong architectural judgment, communication skills, attention to detail, and the ability to balance development speed with correctness and production reliability.

jobs.description:
Crypto Markets Founding Engineer (Python, C++, AI/ML) | Palo Alto | Visa Sponsorship | Up to $300K + Equity

About the company

A 10-person, well-funded startup building AI for markets is hiring three founding engineers. The company trains reasoning systems on social media, Reddit and prediction market data to help its traders read markets faster, and the technology is already live: it trades real money through an internal 8-figure hedge fund anchored by the founder of one of the world's largest proprietary trading firms.

The founding team includes engineers from leading AI labs and a top hedge fund, IMO medalists, and top-ranked crypto and prediction market traders. The company is backed by a $20M seed round led by a top-tier fintech and crypto venture firm, with other well-known funds and angels from prediction markets, fintech and a major Chicago trading firm.

Why crypto and markets engineers should look at this

Crypto runs through this company. The team actively trades crypto and prediction markets, and prediction market data sits at the core of its models. Some prediction markets run on crypto rails and settle in stablecoins onchain, while others are regulated fiat exchanges in the US. This role sits across both worlds, so engineers who understand how onchain markets behave and how regulated venues work will feel right at home.
The investors have a long history backing crypto exchanges, DeFi protocols and onchain analytics firms, and experience at a crypto-native startup or crypto trading firm is explicitly valued.

Unlike most crypto startups, there's no token and no "is this a real business" question. It's a venture-backed company running a live fund.

What you'll build

Data pipelines that turn messy, real-world signals (social, prediction market and market data) into research-ready inputs
Trading signals and the research infrastructure behind them
Automated execution systems and tooling that let the team go from idea to live experiment extremely fast
Systems across trading and HFT infrastructure, security and ML, working directly with quant and AI researchers

You'll take projects from first idea through to production and own them end to end.

Tech stack

Python:
data pipelines, signals and research tooling
C++:
low-latency execution and trading infrastructure
AI/ML:
building and deploying the reasoning models behind the prediction engine

What we're looking for

1 to 5 years of experience as a software engineer or quant developer
Degree in computer science, mathematics, statistics or physics
Exceptional Python or C++
A track record of building and shipping a project end to end, from idea to production, as the owner
Strong statistical intuition and comfort working with noisy real-world data
Experience with AI-driven development
Deep curiosity about markets and the ability to thrive in ambiguity

Backgrounds that stand out

Engineers at crypto trading firms and market makers, especially on execution, data or infrastructure
MEV searchers and DeFi bot builders with real, measurable results
Builders of trading tools, analytics or bots on prediction markets
Onchain data engineers who have also built signals or traded
Early engineers at crypto-native or fintech startups who shipped entire systems
Quant developers, or interns from firms like IMC, Citadel, Jane Street, HRT or Optiver

Exceptional new grads will be considered if they bring real-world exposure such as shipped products, real trading results or serious internships.

This role is not

A Web3 or smart contract role. No Solidity, protocol design or tokens. Crypto here means crypto markets as a trading venue and data source.
A senior or staff position
Frontend, product or business development
Remote or hybrid
Pure ML research. You'll work alongside researchers as the builder.

Location and logistics

Location:
Palo Alto, California
Work arrangement:
fully onsite, 5 to 6 days a week. This is an intense, in-person team.
Relocation:
welcome
Visa:
open to visa transfers (OPT, H1B transfers) and new sponsorships (new H1B, TN). If you're on J1 or O1, mention it when you apply.

Compensation

Up to $300K base plus equity plus performance bonus

Intro call
Technical screen
Take-home
Work trial

A founding seat at a company already trading real capital through an 8-figure fund
Serious backing from top-tier fintech and crypto investors
A tiny, elite team where you own what you build
Crypto, prediction market and trading problems without the token risk
Up to $300K base plus equity, with visa support available

jobs.description:

This is a remote opportunity supporting anticipated federal financial management transformation initiatives within the Department of War.

You will leverage Palantir Foundry and the Vantage platform to modernize financial data, reporting, and decision-making capabilities.

The role combines data engineering, financial management, analytics, and mission-focused technology delivery in a secure environment.

You will work with complex federal financial data, developing pipelines, applications, and analytical solutions that improve transparency and operational effectiveness.

At the Manager level, you will additionally lead multidisciplinary teams, mentor professionals, and influence senior stakeholders.

The opportunity is suited to experienced professionals who enjoy solving complex data challenges and translating technical solutions into meaningful business outcomes.

Accountabilities

Design, develop, and enhance modern financial management solutions within the Vantage platform using Palantir Foundry.
Build and support Foundry-based data solutions, including pipelines, transforms, datasets, data lineage, and related data-processing workflows.

jobs.title: Senior Research Associate, Biology
jobs.description:
At Insmed, every moment and every patient counts — and so does every person who joins in. As a global biopharmaceutical company dedicated to transforming the lives of patients with serious and rare diseases, you’ll be part of a community that prioritizes the human experience, celebrates curiosity, and values every person’s contributions to meaningful progress. That commitment has earned us recognition as Science magazine’s No. 1 Top Employer for five consecutive years, certification as a Great Place to Work® in the U.S., and a place on The Sunday Times Best Places to Work list in the UK.

For patients, for each other, and for the future of science, we’re in. Are you?

About The Role

We’re looking for a Senior Research Associate on the Research Development Laboratory team to help us expand what’s possible for patients with serious diseases. Reporting to the Scientist, you’ll support discovery and development campaigns focused on next-generation biotherapies for serious unmet medical needs.

What You'll Do

In this role, you’ll have the opportunity to work within a multidisciplinary team, conducting molecular biology and protein engineering on a diverse array of biological drug candidates. You’ll also:

Design, execute and optimize molecular biology experiments to support lead candidate selection
Validate and perform DNA based assays (DNA purification, PCR, and Quality and Quantification of DNA)
Culture mammalian cell lines and conduct transient transfections of mammalian cells for protein expression
Culture bacterial cell lines and conduct protein expression and purification
Interact and collaborate with multidisciplinary team to advance the project
Maintain accurate, detailed, and timely records

Who You Are

You have a Master’s degree in Molecular Biology or related field or a Bachelor’s degree in Molecular Biology or related field with minimum 2 years of experience.

You Are Or You Also Have

Requires hands-on experience with routine molecular biology methods including plasmid cloning, PCR, and DNA isolation and protein expression
Organizational skills and ability to prioritize multiple tasks

Nice To Have (but Not Required)

Hands-on experience with tissue culture, protein purification, enzyme assay, gel electrophoresis, and flow cytometry are strongly preferred
Proficiency with SNAPgene, GraphPad Prism/Excel, and relevant scientific software is desirable
Experience with library preparation for NGS, DNA and RNA quality and quantification methods (TapeStation and Qubit) is desirable but not required
Experience with protein binding kinetics assays (BLI, SPR, and ELISA) is desirable but not required

Where You’ll Work

This role is based out of our New Hampshire Research Development Laboratory
and requires full-time, in-person presence
to support hands-on collaboration, access specialized equipment, and/or operational needs.

Travel Requirements

Minimal travel expected

Pay Range

$80,000.00-102,000.00 Annual

Life at Insmed

Company Learning Institute providing access to LinkedIn Learning, skill building workshops, leadership programs, mentorship connections, and networking opportunities

jobs.description:
Overview

Susquehanna's Sell Side Equity Research Department is looking for talent that wants to be a part of a ranked research platform. In order to continue the success of delivering a differentiated research product, we are looking for an Sell Side Research Associate to provide research support for the technology space in our New York office. The role will be mentored by a well-known Senior Analyst. The job offers excellent exposure to emerging growth companies in the tech sector and provides a strong career path in sell-side Equity research, asset management, and business development/corporate strategy.

In This Role, You Will

Provide primary analytical support for the Senior Analyst covering the space
Conduct proprietary research, customer/partner interviews and industry surveys
Perform financial and valuation analysis by generating financial models/forecasts and competitive profiles on companies under coverage
Gather and analyze data from a variety of sources, including, but not limited to, company documents and materials, SEC/regulatory filings (annual reports, 10-K’s 10-Q’s, etc.), industry publications, trade shows, and online data services
Interact with company management, internal sales force, and institutional investors
Monitor and evaluate company news and events
Perform other related duties, as assigned

What We're Looking For

2+ years of (analytical) work experience in such fields as finance/accounting and/or engineering.
Prior equity research (sell/buy side) a plus
Knowledge of the technology sector (Hardware, Software, Internet), a plus
Series 7, 63, 86 and/or 87 a plus, but not required
Passion for the markets, passion for a career in equity research, illustration this through prior school projects and/or work experience a plus
Illustrating a desire to pursue a career in sell side equity research a plus
Excellent research, writing, communication, and organization skills; candidates must be extremely detail oriented
Working knowledge of Microsoft products (Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint and Word)
Independent thinker and self-starter with the motivation to learn about and excel in a dynamic industry
Will not require sponsorship for work authorization now or in the future
